newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's largest state sets December election.
newsitem.headline: Australia's largest state sets December election.

text.p: Australia's largest state, Western Australia, will go to the polls on December 14, the state government said on Thursday.
The election in Western Australia, where outback desert occupies an area almost the size of Argentina, will be the state's first pre-Christmas poll in 50 years.

The conservative Liberal-National government headed by state premier Richard Court is well ahead in opinion polls and is expected to retain control of the lower house of parliament, say political analysts. But there is an outside chance the 106-year conservative reign in the upper house may end.

The election will be fought largely on local issues in a state which boasts one of the country's largest aboriginal populations and some of its biggest gold and diamond mines and oil and gas reserves.
Conservative governments are now in power nationally in Australia and in five of the country's six states and both its autonomous territories.
